question: According to the programme set out by the Belgian Presidency of the Council of the European Union, one of the priorities for the semester is to improve knowledge valorisation in Europe, which is at the forefront of research and innovation in many fields. One of the EU’s biggest problems is the ‘European innovation paradox’, i.e.

the challenge of transferring skills and innovations to viable projects that lead to economic and social growth. One of the main obstacles to overcoming this paradox is the ‘valley of death’ phenomenon, which is the period when a company that has come up with an innovative concept has yet to see an economic return on it.

That period can last quite some time and can thus be a disincentive in the application of innovation and research. In view of this: What measures will the Commission take to improve knowledge and skills valorisation in Europe?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.3.2024) The Commission strives to strengthen knowledge valorisation to maximise the impact of all knowledge assets generated by researchers and innovators in the EU. In 2022, following the Commission’s proposal, the Council adopted a Recommendation on the guiding principles for knowledge valorisation1.

The Recommendation aims to increase economic and societal value creation from research and to make innovation more inclusive. It puts the emphasis on fostering an entrepreneurial mindset for students and researchers by investing in education and skills. It also encourages links and co-creation between different actors.

The guiding principles are supported by Commission Recommendations on codes of practice on the management of intellectual assets for knowledge valorisation and on standardisation in the European Research Area2 providing hands-on guidance on specific knowledge valorisation areas to support the swift market uptake of results.

Increasing knowledge valorisation is also embedded in Horizon Europe3 with legal obligations on dissemination and exploitation of results4, and support services for EU-funded beneficiaries, such as the Horizon Results Booster5 and Horizon Results Platform6. Moreover, the Commission is raising awareness on knowledge valorisation through the ongoing campaign7 in Member States.

The Commission attaches the highest importance to researchers’ transversal skills, including those related to knowledge valorisation. It has developed the European Competence Framework for Researchers (ResearchComp)8, which fosters the development and recognition of researchers’ transversal skills and will improve inter-sectoral mobility and knowledge valorisation.

ResearchComp will be key in encouraging researchers to cooperate more with industry to the benefit of innovation.
